questions.q: Acetaldehyde reacts with nitromethane in the presence of a catalytic amount of OH⁻ at room temperature. The product is:
questions.explain: The nitronate carbon bonds to the carbonyl carbon and C=O becomes C–OH, giving CH₃CH(OH)CH₂NO₂, a β-nitro alcohol. 3-Hydroxybutanal would be the ordinary aldol product of acetaldehyde with itself.

questions.q: Only a catalytic amount of a weak base is needed to deprotonate nitromethane in the Henry reaction because:
options: the C–H next to –NO₂ has a pKa of about 9, as the nitronate charge is delocalised onto both nitro oxygens
nitromethane is a stronger acid than HCl
the nitro nitrogen carries a lone pair that takes up the proton
the base is regenerated only after dehydration
questions.explain: A C–H next to a nitro group (pKa about 9) is far more acidic than an aldehyde α-H (about 17) or ketone α-H (about 20), because the nitronate ion is resonance-stabilised. OH⁻ is regenerated when the alkoxide is protonated.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde and nitromethane are heated with excess base. The final product is:
questions.explain: The β-nitro alcohol still has hydrogens on the nitro-bearing carbon, so heating or excess base removes water to give the conjugated nitroalkene, β-nitrostyrene.

questions.q: The Henry product of acetaldehyde and nitromethane is reduced with H₂ over a catalyst. The product is:
questions.explain: Reducing the –NO₂ group of a β-nitro alcohol gives a β-amino alcohol, here CH₃CH(OH)CH₂NH₂. Oxidising the OH instead would give the α-nitro ketone.
